milestones.title: Paulo Dias de Novais founds Luanda
milestones.detail: The Portuguese captain founded São Paulo da Assunção de Loanda on 25 January 1576, bringing about a hundred settler families and four hundred soldiers. The Fortress of São Miguel was begun on the hill above the bay the same year.
milestones.source: A. R. Disney (2009), A History of Portugal and the Portuguese Empire, vol. 2, p. 72, via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luanda

milestones.title: Settlement recognised as a city
milestones.detail: Luanda was given the status of a city in 1605.
milestones.source: Catarina Madeira Santos (2008), 'Luanda', in L. M. Brockey (ed.), Portuguese Colonial Cities in the Early Modern World, via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Luanda

milestones.title: Administrative centre of Portuguese Angola
milestones.detail: From 1627 Luanda was the seat of the colony's administration and Portugal's bridgehead in Angola.

milestones.title: Captured by the Dutch
milestones.detail: The Dutch captured the city in 1641 and held it under the name Fort Aardenburgh.
milestones.source: W. Martin James (2011), Historical Dictionary of Angola, 2nd ed., via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Luanda

milestones.title: Retaken by Portugal
milestones.detail: Salvador Correia de Sá recovered the city for Portugal in 1648, ending the Dutch occupation.

milestones.title: Fortress of São Francisco do Penedo built
milestones.detail: The third of the city's forts was built in 1765-66, while Luanda was the main port of the slave trade to Brazil.

milestones.title: Slave exports declared illegal
milestones.detail: Portugal banned the export slave trade in 1836, ending the business on which the city had lived for more than two centuries.
milestones.source: José C. Curto (1999), International Journal of African Historical Studies 32(2/3), via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Luanda

milestones.title: Port opened to foreign shipping
milestones.detail: Angola's ports were opened to foreign ships in 1844. Trade in palm oil, wax, ivory and coffee grew, and the city's population more than doubled by 1850.
milestones.source: José C. Curto (1999), International Journal of African Historical Studies 32(2/3), via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Luanda

milestones.title: Aqueduct and railway open
milestones.detail: Governor Brito Capelo opened an aqueduct that gave the city a regular water supply, and the Luanda Railway into the interior began operating.

milestones.title: Airport inaugurated
milestones.detail: The General Craveiro Lopes Airport was inaugurated in 1954, as the city grew quickly under the Estado Novo.

milestones.title: Capital of independent Angola
milestones.detail: Angola became independent on 11 November 1975 as civil war began. Most of the Portuguese population left, and war refugees began to swell the musseques around the city.
milestones.source: Patrick Chabal (ed.) (2002), A History of Postcolonial Lusophone Africa, via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Luanda

milestones.title: Three Day War
milestones.detail: From 30 October to 1 November 1992 fighting between government and UNITA forces broke out in the city after disputed elections.

milestones.title: Civil war ends and rebuilding begins
milestones.detail: The end of the civil war in 2002 and rising oil income started a period of major reconstruction of roads, housing and the bay front.
milestones.source: The Economist, 'Marching towards riches and democracy?' (28 August 2008), via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luanda

milestones.title: Kilamba new town and Neto memorial completed
milestones.detail: The Kilamba housing development was built near the city, and the Agostinho Neto memorial, begun in 1982, was inaugurated on 17 September 2012.

landmarks.note: Coordinates from OpenStreetMap (building named 'Sonangol' off Rua Rainha Ginga); approximate.

landmarks.name: Torre Ambiente
landmarks.note: CTBUH marks the 117 m height as estimated from the floor count (30 floors); Wikipedia, citing SkyscraperPage, gives 102 m. Coordinates from OpenStreetMap.

landmarks.name: Memorial Dr. António Agostinho Neto (mausoleum spire)
landmarks.note: Concrete spire begun in 1982, structurally complete in January 2011 and inaugurated on 17 September 2012. Wikipedia gives the 120 m height without a citation; press reports repeat it.

landmarks.note: CTBUH gives completion in 2014; Wikipedia's list gives 2011. Coordinates from OpenStreetMap.

landmarks.name: IMOB Business Tower
landmarks.note: Tallest building in Angola. The building could not be found on OpenStreetMap; the coordinates are a point on its street, Rua Major Kanhangulo, and may be off by a few hundred metres.

notes: Start date: 1576 is well documented and not contested; the Wikipedia timeline also lists an unsourced church on the Ilha de Luanda in 1575. Population: nothing was found for the first two centuries (1576-1780); the only early figure seen is the founding party of about a hundred families and four hundred soldiers, which is not a population count, so no point is given at the start year. From 1781 to 1844 Luanda has an unusually good series of colonial censuses, published by Curto and Gervais; eleven of their counts are used here (the table has more years). These count residents of the city, free and enslaved, and show a real decline from 1781 to 1817. After 1850 the series is thin again: only a round estimate from the 1911 Britannica and the 1940 census were found, so 1850-1940 is a ninety-year gap with one soft point. The 1940 figure appears as 61,028 and 61,208 in different places. Landmarks: every entry is from 2007 or later. No sourced height was found for any of the historic monuments, so these were left out: Fortaleza de São Miguel (1576), Fortaleza de São Pedro da Barra (1618), Igreja de Nossa Senhora da Nazaré, the cathedral (Igreja dos Remédios, 1679), Palácio de Ferro (1890s), Banco Nacional de Angola (1956), Estádio 11 de Novembro (2009) and the National Assembly. Torre Ambiente's height is a CTBUH estimate. Coordinates for the towers are from OpenStreetMap; the IMOB tower's are street-level only.
